title: FlashCart — the bus and the gate

panels.title: Oldest unpublished message (seconds)
panels.description: The number that actually matters. Depth alone cannot tell a busy relay from a dead one — under a flash sale a deep queue is correct. An old row never is.

panels.title: Outbox depth
panels.description: Queued messages awaiting the relay. A steady small number is normal under load; a line that only climbs is a relay that has stopped.

panels.title: Relay throughput vs send failures
panels.description: A single poisoned row retried every tick climbs the failure line while depth stays at one — a different shape from a broker outage.

panels.title: The availability gate — is it earning its place?
Gate decisions
panels.description: REFUSED is the gate's entire reason to exist: requests answered without touching a connection. If it stays near zero under load, the gate is pure overhead. A sustained UNKNOWN rate means Redis is unreachable and the gate is doing nothing — while the platform stays perfectly correct, because PostgreSQL still decides.

panels.title: Share of requests refused before the database
panels.description: The gate's payoff, as a fraction. Everything else still reached PostgreSQL, where the conditional UPDATE decided it.

panels.title: The saga — where orders are going
Order transitions
panels.description: Tagged from → to, so the compensation paths are legible without reading the code. PAYMENT_PENDING → PAYMENT_FAILED and RESERVED → RESERVATION_EXPIRED are the two that say the platform is losing orders, and to what.

panels.title: Transitions the state machine declined
panels.description: Should sit at zero. Since Phase 8, duplicates are caught by processed_events before reaching the guard, so anything here is a transition that was genuinely attempted and should not have been.
